page: UpCloud PREMIUM-16xCPU-64GB is a balanced general-purpose cloud instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, delivering 16 virtual CPUs mapping to 16 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. The system integrates 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled as a 300 GB SSD, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. The configuration includes no discrete graphics processing hardware.

Hardware vector and instruction set capabilities include AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), AVX-VNNI, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, while AMX support is absent. In synthetic benchmarking, the single-core performance registers strongly, attaining a Geekbench single-core score of 2,562.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 39.49 GB/sec, placing it within the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. Multi-core execution demonstrates consistent capacity, recording 16,682.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 44,425.64 in multi-core stress-ng tests. PassMark evaluations show balanced results, with an overall CPU score of 35,388.02 and a database operations mark of 12,422.48.

Data throughput metrics reveal an uncached large block memory read bandwidth of 147.28 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 62.48 GB/sec. Application benchmarks reflect standard shared-instance outputs, such as Redis SET throughput reaching 25.98 million operations per second and static web serving hitting 21.01 GB/sec. Large language model inference on CPU yields 557.46 tokens per second for small-model prompt processing, but sequential text generation is limited, bottoming out at 9.08 tokens per second for small models.

UpCloud PREMIUM-16xCPU-64GB delivers strong per-core instruction throughput and steady aggregate computing power, presenting a viable resource profile for production web backends, CI/CD compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters, relational database hosting, and ETL data transformations that do not depend on GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core compute performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,562.0 and rapid single-threaded gzip compression at 39.49 GB/sec, paired with solid multi-core output (16,682.0 Geekbench multi-core score). With memory read bandwidth of 147.28 GB/sec and static web serving throughput reaching 21.01 GB/sec, this server fits general web applications, relational databases, caching layers, software compilation, and mid-tier analytical pipelines.
